title: Number of Islands
prompt: Given an `m x n` 2D binary `grid` where `"1"` represents land and `"0"` represents water, return the number of islands. An island is surrounded by water and formed by connecting adjacent lands horizontally or vertically.

examples.explanation: The top-left 1s form one connected island; the bottom-right 1 is a separate island.

hints: Scan every cell. When you find a '1' you haven't visited, that's a new island — increment your count.
From that cell, flood-fill (DFS or BFS) to every connected '1', marking each as visited so it isn't counted again.
You can mark visited cells by mutating the grid in place (e.g. setting them to '0') instead of a separate visited set, if you don't need to preserve the input.

solution.approach: Iterate every cell in the grid. Whenever a '1' is found, it must be part of an island not yet counted, so increment the island count and run a DFS/BFS flood-fill from that cell, marking every connected '1' as visited (flipped to '0') so the outer scan skips them. This ensures each island is counted exactly once.
